data.content_ref: inline:SRC_003 anchors its distinction on RFC 9110 §9.2.1, where 'safe' means read-only/no side effects—an HTTP method-semantics definition. But the problem concerns deterministic replay in an append-only reasoning system with at-least-once delivery: a distributed-systems context in which 'safe' conventionally means retry-safe (no harmful effect from repetition), not 'read-only.' Under the retry-safe reading, an append IS safe (duplicate entries cause no corruption), and the log does require safe writers—which is exactly the answer SRC_003's own first countercondition concedes ('If the problem uses safe in the retry-safety sense ... the log does require safe (retry-safe) writers'). The problem's framing (at-least-once delivery, replay, retried operations) clearly invokes retry-safety, not HTTP method categorization. By choosing RFC 9110's read-only definition as primary, SRC_003 answers a different question and lands on 'neither,' when the relevant published distributed-systems notion of 'safe' directly applies to the writers the problem asks about.
